findings.summary: `CompletionItemKind` in type_utils.jac declares all 25 LSP completion-kind constants, but only 6 are ever referenced. The sole consumer is `completion_kind_from_sym` in type_system/impl/type_utils.impl.jac:303-322, whose match returns exactly Module, Function, Class, Enum, Variable, and Text. I grepped the whole repo for `CompletionItemKind\.\w+` and got 8 hits total: those 6 in type_utils.impl.jac, plus `lspt.CompletionItemKind.Keyword` in jaclang/langserve/impl/engine.impl.jac:611 and `lspt.CompletionItemKind.Variable` in a tool fixture — both of which resolve to the *separate* LSP enum defined at jac/jaclang/lsp/types.jac:62, not this one. The remaining 19 members (Method, Constructor, Field, Interface, Property, Unit, Value, Keyword, Snippet, Color, File, Reference, Folder, EnumMember, Constant, Struct, Event, Operator, TypeParameter) have zero references anywhere in the tree. Judgement is needed because the numeric values must stay LSP-spec-aligned for the 6 that remain, so the surviving members must keep their current integer literals rather than being renumbered.

`TypeCategory.Unbound` (types.jac:9) is declared but never referenced. I grepped the whole repo for `TypeCategory\.\w+` and collected every occurrence: Unknown, Never, Any, Module, TypeVar, Class, Function, Overload, Union and EnumMember all appear as `CATEGORY` ClassVar assignments in types.jac plus reads in type_evaluator.impl/type_evaluator.impl.jac:2637 and type_system/impl/types.impl.jac:439-513 — `Unbound` appears nowhere but its own declaration line. No `TypeBase` subclass sets `CATEGORY = TypeCategory.Unbound`, so no type value can ever carry it. Because the enum is an `IntEnum` with implicit auto-numbering, deleting the first member shifts every subsequent member's integer value, so this needs a human to confirm nothing serializes these ordinals (JIR caches, .jir sections) before removing it.
